summary: Found multiple critical vulnerabilities including reentrancy in contribute() and fulfillRandomWords(), double payment bug, logic error in contribution validation, and VRF callback DoS vector.

findings.title: Reentrancy in contribute() function
findings.description: The contribute() function makes an external call to group.contributionAddress.call{value: amount}() at line 269, then calls receiveContributionContract.receiveContributionData() at line 270, and only then updates state variables (hasContributed, hasContributedTime, currentRoundContributedContributors) at lines 274-277. If contributionAddress is a malicious contract, it can re-enter contribute() before state is updated, allowing double-contribution or manipulation of round accounting.
findings.attack_scenario: 1. Attacker creates a group with a malicious contract as contributionAddress (via owner setAddress or if owner is compromised). 2. Attacker calls contribute() with valid amount. 3. Malicious contributionAddress re-enters contribute() via fallback/receive. 4. Since hasContributed[attacker][id] is still false, the re-entrant call passes checks and processes again. 5. Attacker gets counted twice in currentRoundContributedContributors, potentially triggering AllContributedForCurrentRound prematurely and manipulating winner selection.

findings.title: Double payment in fulfillRandomWords()
findings.description: Line 348 calls _contract.withdraw(groupId) which sends group.payout to the Contribution contract (msg.sender in withdraw is the Contribution contract). Line 349 then sends group.payout again to the winner. This pays out 2x the intended amount: once to the Contribution contract (which holds it) and once to the winner.
findings.attack_scenario: 1. Normal group operation proceeds to winner selection. 2. fulfillRandomWords is called via VRF callback. 3. withdraw() sends payout to Contribution contract balance. 4. winner.call sends same payout to winner. 5. Contract loses double the funds; owner can withdraw the excess via withdraw() function (line 390-393).

findings.title: Logic error in contribution amount validation
findings.description: The condition `if (msg.value == 0 && msg.value < group.amount)` is logically incorrect. It only reverts when msg.value is exactly 0. Any positive value (including 1 wei or values greater than group.amount) passes validation. Contributors can underpay or overpay.
findings.attack_scenario: 1. Contributor calls contribute() with msg.value = 1 wei (far less than group.amount). 2. Check passes because msg.value != 0. 3. Contribution is recorded as valid, attacker gets counted in currentRoundContributedContributors. 4. If all contributors underpay, AllContributedForCurrentRound triggers with insufficient funds. 5. Winner receives full payout from contract balance (which is less than expected), draining contract or causing shortfall.

findings.title: VRF callback DoS via winner.call revert
findings.description: The winner payout uses `winner.call{value: group.payout}("")` with `require(success, "payout not successful")`. If the winner is a smart contract that reverts on receive (e.g., fallback reverts, or gas limit too low), the entire VRF callback reverts. Since VRF callbacks cannot be retried with different parameters, this permanently bricks the group - no winner can be paid, upkeep cannot complete, and funds are locked.
findings.attack_scenario: 1. Attacker becomes a contributor in a group (or convinces victim to add attacker's malicious contract as contributor). 2. When attacker wins, their contract's receive/fallback reverts. 3. fulfillRandomWords reverts, VRF callback fails. 4. Group is permanently stuck: UpkeepNeededForGroups remains true, but performUpkeep will keep requesting VRF for same group, each callback reverting. 5. Funds contributed by all participants are locked forever.

findings.title: s_contributionAddress can be address(0) causing failed contributions
findings.description: s_contributionAddress is only set via owner-only setAddress(). If owner never calls it, s_contributionAddress defaults to address(0). createContributionGroup stores this zero address in the group's contributionAddress. Later contribute() calls will attempt to call address(0) at line 269, which will fail (success=false) and revert at line 272.
findings.attack_scenario: 1. Owner deploys contract but forgets to call setAddress(). 2. Users create groups and contribute. 3. All contribute() calls revert with "Contribution failed". 4. Funds sent with contribute() are returned (call to address(0) returns false, require reverts, msg.value refunded). 5. Protocol is unusable until owner sets address.

findings.title: performUpkeep processes only one group per call, causing starvation
findings.description: checkUpkeep only returns the first element of s_UpkeepNeededGroupIds (line 295). performUpkeep processes that single group and removes it from the array (lines 326-327). If multiple groups need upkeep, only one is processed per Automation upkeep call. Groups added later wait indefinitely if Automation doesn't call frequently enough, delaying winner selection and payouts.
findings.attack_scenario: 1. Many groups reach AllContributedForCurrentRound simultaneously. 2. All their IDs are pushed to s_UpkeepNeededGroupIds. 3. Chainlink Automation calls performUpkeep periodically (e.g., every 30 min). 4. Only one group processed per call; others wait. 5. If new groups keep being added, older groups may wait hours/days for winner selection. 6. Contributors' funds are locked during this delay.
